# package link

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-canbus/socketcan/link"
```

Package link reads and changes the configuration of Linux CAN network interfaces through rtnetlink, the interface ip-link(8) uses: listing CAN interfaces, their state, bit timing, CAN FD data bit timing, control modes, error counters and statistics; bringing them up and down; setting bit rates, CAN FD mode, restart-ms and MTU; restarting a bus-off controller; creating and deleting vcan and vxcan interfaces.

It is an administrative API, kept apart from the transports on purpose: opening a socket never reconfigures an interface. Reading needs no privileges; changes need CAP\_NET\_ADMIN, and the kernel rejects bit timing changes while an interface is up (EBUSY) and on virtual interfaces, which have no bit timing (EOPNOTSUPP).

On systems other than Linux every function returns [canbus.ErrUnsupported](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canbus#ErrUnsupported).

## Functions

### func AddVCAN

```go
func AddVCAN(name string, fd bool) error
```

AddVCAN creates a vcan interface with the CAN FD MTU (72) when fd is set, else the classical MTU (16). (The kernel's own default differs between versions: 72, or 2060 since CAN XL.)

### func AddVXCAN

```go
func AddVXCAN(name, peer string) error
```

AddVXCAN creates a vxcan tunnel: two interfaces, name and peer, where a frame sent on one is received on the other. Moving the peer into another network namespace connects two namespaces (containers).

### func Configure

```go
func Configure(name string, cfg Config) error
```

Configure applies bit timing, control modes and restart-ms to a CAN controller interface. The interface must be down. vcan and vxcan interfaces have no bit timing: the kernel reports EOPNOTSUPP, returned as [canbus.ErrUnsupported](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canbus#ErrUnsupported).

### func Delete

```go
func Delete(name string) error
```

Delete deletes an interface (for example one made by AddVCAN).

### func Restart

```go
func Restart(name string) error
```

Restart restarts a controller that is bus-off (IFLA\_CAN\_RESTART).

### func SetDown

```go
func SetDown(name string) error
```

SetDown brings the interface down.

### func SetMTU

```go
func SetMTU(name string, mtu int) error
```

SetMTU sets the MTU: 16 for classical CAN, 72 for CAN FD. Controllers accept 72 only in CAN FD mode.

### func SetUp

```go
func SetUp(name string) error
```

SetUp brings the interface up.

## Types

### type BitTiming

```go
type BitTiming struct {
	Bitrate     uint32 `json:"bitrate"`
	SamplePoint uint32 `json:"samplePoint"`
	TQ          uint32 `json:"tq"`
	PropSeg     uint32 `json:"propSeg"`
	PhaseSeg1   uint32 `json:"phaseSeg1"`
	PhaseSeg2   uint32 `json:"phaseSeg2"`
	SJW         uint32 `json:"sjw"`
	BRP         uint32 `json:"brp"`
}
```

BitTiming is struct can\_bittiming. SamplePoint is in tenths of a percent (875 = 87.5 %), as the kernel reports it.

### type Config

```go
type Config struct {
	Bitrate         uint32 // nominal bit rate in bit/s
	SamplePoint     uint32 // nominal sample point in tenths of a percent (0: driver default)
	DataBitrate     uint32 // CAN FD data bit rate in bit/s
	DataSamplePoint uint32
	// Modes to switch on (Set) and off (Clear), for example ModeFD.
	Set, Clear CtrlMode
	RestartMs  *uint32
}
```

Config is a set of changes for [Configure](#func-configure). Nil and zero fields are left unchanged.

#### func (Config) Empty

```go
func (c *Config) Empty() bool
```

Empty reports a Config without changes.

### type ControllerState

```go
type ControllerState uint32
```

ControllerState is the CAN controller state (IFLA\_CAN\_STATE).

```go
const (
	StateErrorActive ControllerState = iota
	StateErrorWarning
	StateErrorPassive
	StateBusOff
	StateStopped
	StateSleeping
)
```

Controller states (enum can\_state).

#### func (ControllerState) String

```go
func (s ControllerState) String() string
```

String names the state as ip-link does.

### type CtrlMode

```go
type CtrlMode uint32
```

CtrlMode is a set of CAN controller modes (CAN\_CTRLMODE\_\*).

```go
const (
	ModeLoopback      CtrlMode = 0x001
	ModeListenOnly    CtrlMode = 0x002
	ModeTripleSample  CtrlMode = 0x004
	ModeOneShot       CtrlMode = 0x008
	ModeBerrReporting CtrlMode = 0x010
	ModeFD            CtrlMode = 0x020
	ModePresumeAck    CtrlMode = 0x040
	ModeFDNonISO      CtrlMode = 0x080
	ModeCCLen8DLC     CtrlMode = 0x100
	ModeTDCAuto       CtrlMode = 0x200
	ModeTDCManual     CtrlMode = 0x400
)
```

Controller modes.

#### func (CtrlMode) String

```go
func (m CtrlMode) String() string
```

String lists the modes, for example "FD,BERR-REPORTING".

### type Interface

```go
type Interface struct {
	Name       string `json:"name"`
	Index      int    `json:"index"`
	Kind       string `json:"kind"` // "can" (a controller driver), "vcan", "vxcan", or "" when the kernel does not say
	Up         bool   `json:"up"`
	OperState  string `json:"operState"`
	MTU        int    `json:"mtu"` // 16 classical, 72 CAN FD, 2060 CAN XL (Linux ≥ 6.2)
	TxQueueLen int    `json:"txQueueLen"`
	Stats      Stats  `json:"stats"`

	// Controller details, for kind "can" only.
	State             *ControllerState `json:"state,omitempty"`
	BitTiming         *BitTiming       `json:"bitTiming,omitempty"`
	DataBitTiming     *BitTiming       `json:"dataBitTiming,omitempty"`
	ClockHz           uint32           `json:"clockHz,omitempty"`
	CtrlModeSupported CtrlMode         `json:"ctrlModeSupported,omitempty"`
	CtrlMode          CtrlMode         `json:"ctrlMode,omitempty"`
	RestartMs         *uint32          `json:"restartMs,omitempty"`
	ErrorCounters     *ErrorCounters   `json:"errorCounters,omitempty"`
	DeviceStats       *DeviceStats     `json:"deviceStats,omitempty"`
}
```

Interface describes a CAN network interface.

```go
func Get(name string) (Interface, error)
```

```go

```

#### func (Interface) FD

```go
func (i *Interface) FD() bool
```

FD reports whether the interface carries CAN FD frames: its MTU is the CAN FD MTU (72) or the CAN XL MTU (2060).


Virtual reports a vcan or vxcan interface.
